definition: A network bringing primary and secondary schools together.
plain: A network that brings primary and secondary schools together.

definition: A global mining business.
plain: A global mining business.
note: Companies House: Anglo American plc, 03564138 (the global parent company).

term: Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings
full_term: Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings
definition: The Office for National Statistics' official survey of earnings.
plain: The official survey of what people earn.

definition: An award-winning primary careers and enrichment programme run in Redcar & Cleveland since 2021 by RCVDA.
plain: An award-winning primary careers and enrichment programme, run in Redcar & Cleveland since 2021.

definition: A termly network of local employers who help shape and run the programme.
plain: A network of local employers who help shape and run the programme. It meets each term.

definition: A mentoring role in which a career champion supports a school.
plain: A mentor scheme: a career champion supports a school.

definition: Pupil Journey step 1: exploring what a career is and what jobs exist in the local area.
plain: What a career is, and what jobs there are in the local area.

definition: The teacher responsible for careers learning at a school.
plain: The teacher in charge of careers learning at a school.

definition: Careers-related learning — the careers learning taught in schools.
plain: The careers lessons taught in school.

definition: A short termly write-up of impact telling one pupil's or one school's story.
plain: A short write-up of impact, one each term. It tells one pupil's or one school's story.

definition: A careers framework for Key Stage 2 (ages 7 to 11) produced by the Career Development Institute.
plain: A careers framework for Key Stage 2 (ages 7 to 11), made by the Career Development Institute.

definition: An offshore wind farm off the North East coast of England.
plain: A large wind farm out at sea, off the North East coast.
note: Dogger Bank Wind Farm is a legal partnership / joint venture, not a single registered company, so it has no one org reference.

definition: The statutory stage of learning and development for children from birth to age 5.
plain: The stage for the youngest children.
source: DfE — Statutory framework for the early years foundation stage

definition: The sector's terms for pupils meeting the world of work.
plain: The words the sector uses for pupils meeting the world of work.

definition: Pupil Journey step 6: real interviews with business partners, followed by feedback.
plain: Real interviews with business partners, then feedback.

definition: Extra activities beyond the six Pupil Journey steps, such as Parliament Week and science and technology events.
plain: Extra activities beyond the six steps. They include Parliament Week and science and technology events.

definition: A Norwegian energy company; one of the three owners of Dogger Bank Wind Farm and its operator.
plain: One of the three owners of Dogger Bank Wind Farm, and the one that runs it.
note: Norwegian company — not registered in England & Wales, so no Companies House / FTC reference.

definition: Pupil Journey step 2: teaching the eight essential skills from the Skills Builder Universal Framework.
plain: The eight essential skills from the Skills Builder Universal Framework.

definition: The national standard of eight benchmarks for good careers guidance.
plain: The national standard for good careers guidance.

definition: A national measure of the proportion of children in an area living in income-deprived households.
plain: A measure of child poverty in an area.

definition: Pupil Journey step 5: body language and speaking well at work.
plain: Body language and how to speak well at work.

definition: An award scheme recognising good primary careers work; three schools are working towards it.
plain: An award for good primary careers work. Three schools are working towards it now.

definition: The stage of the national curriculum for pupils in school years 3 to 6 (roughly ages 7 to 11).
plain: The primary years, roughly ages 7 to 11.

definition: One of the three core themes of the PSHE Association's programme of study, covering careers and the world of work.
plain: One of the three main parts of the PSHE Association's plan of study.

definition: A teaching approach using role-play and inquiry, in which pupils take on the role of experts.
plain: A way of teaching through role-play and inquiry.

definition: Pupil Journey step 3: a first meeting with a local business or project.
plain: A first meeting with a local business or project.

definition: A separate Dogger Bank Wind Farm grant scheme giving up to £1,000 to community groups.
plain: A separate Dogger Bank Wind Farm grant scheme. It gives up to £1,000 to community groups.

definition: Research (Percy and Mann, 2014) on the relationship between skills and future pay.
plain: Research on how skills affect future pay.

definition: A termly survey run before and after the work to measure changes in how pupils explore careers.
plain: A survey run each term, before and after the work. It measures changes in how pupils explore careers.

definition: The programme's main delivery network, meeting each term.
plain: The main delivery network. It meets each term.

definition: A network supporting the move up to secondary school.
plain: A network that supports the move up to secondary school.

definition: A skills framework built around eight essential skills for work and life.
plain: A skills framework built around eight essential skills.

definition: The framework of support for children and young people with special educational needs or disabilities.
plain: Extra support for pupils with special educational needs or disabilities.

definition: A renewable-energy company that owns 40% of Dogger Bank Wind Farm.
plain: A renewable-energy company. It owns 40% of Dogger Bank Wind Farm.
note: Companies House: SSE plc, SC117119 (the parent group; SSE Renewables is its renewables arm).

definition: The part of Dogger Bank Wind Farm's community giving that funds Building our Futures.
plain: The part of Dogger Bank Wind Farm's community giving that pays for Building our Futures.

definition: Pupil Journey step 4: a problem-solving or design challenge set by an employer.
plain: A problem to solve or a design challenge, set by an employer.

definition: The eight skills for work and life set out in the Skills Builder Universal Framework.
plain: The eight skills for work and life, set out in the Skills Builder Universal Framework.

definition: The six-step framework at the heart of Building our Futures, delivered in primary schools for children aged 7 to 11.
plain: The six steps at the heart of the programme. It runs in primary schools for children aged 7 to 11.

definition: Work that supports pupils moving from primary to secondary school.
plain: Work that helps pupils move from primary to secondary school.

definition: An offshore-wind company that owns 20% of Dogger Bank Wind Farm.
plain: An offshore-wind company. It owns 20% of Dogger Bank Wind Farm.
note: Norwegian company — not registered in England & Wales, so no Companies House / FTC reference.

definition: National domestic-abuse charity that develops and stewards the evidence base and models for the high-risk response, including the Multi-Agency Risk Assessment Conference (MARAC) and the Independent Domestic Violence Advisor (IDVA) models. Known as Co-ordinated Action Against Domestic Abuse (CAADA) until it was renamed SafeLives in 2014.
note: Added 2026-08-13: SafeLives previously appeared only as a source (MARAC steward; IDVA source), with no entry of its own. CAADA is the former name of the organisation; the 2010 report Saving lives, saving money cited in the DA report was published under CAADA. Pending team sign-off.

definition: The operating name since 2019 of the Big Lottery Fund: the UK's largest funder of community activity, distributing money raised for good causes by National Lottery players. Joint funder of Changing Futures with MHCLG.
source: National Lottery Act 2006 (established the Big Lottery Fund, which has operated as The National Lottery Community Fund since 2019).
note: Added 2026-08-13: co-funder of Changing Futures, previously written out in full everywhere with no entry of its own; now abbreviated TNLCF across the report series. Pending team sign-off.

definition: The UK government department responsible for the courts, prisons, probation and sentencing policy in England and Wales; commissioned the Intensive Supervision Courts pilot and published the process evaluation cited in the Multiple Disadvantage report.
note: Added 2026-08-13: previously used only as the abbreviation MoJ across the reports with no entry of its own. Pending team sign-off.

definition: The framework used to assess, plan and coordinate care for people with more complex mental-health needs; now largely superseded by the Community Mental Health Framework.
source: Department of Health — Care Programme Approach.
note: Being replaced by the Community Mental Health Framework (from 2019).

term: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services
full_term: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services
definition: NHS services that assess and treat children and young people with emotional, behavioural or mental-health difficulties.
Collective term for children and young people, commonly used in health, education and social-care services.

full_term: Children and Young People’s Improving Access to Psychological Therapies programme
definition: An NHS England programme to transform children and young people's mental-health services by embedding evidence-based psychological therapies and outcome monitoring.
The NHS bodies that commissioned most local health services from 2013; abolished in July 2022 and replaced by Integrated Care Boards (ICBs).
note: Superseded by ICB (Health and Care Act 2022).

definition: The transfer of land or buildings from public ownership (usually a local authority) to a community or voluntary organisation, at less than market value, to secure community benefit.

A notice requiring a person or body to stop or take action about behaviour that is unreasonable and has a detrimental effect on the local community's quality of life. Distinct from Community Psychiatric Nurse (also 'CPN').
source: Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014, s.43
note: Homonym: not Community Psychiatric Nurse (see community-psychiatric-nurse).

definition: A registered mental-health nurse who supports people with mental-health needs in the community; now more often titled community mental-health nurse.
A statutory partnership of local 'responsible authorities' (police, local authority, fire, health and probation) that works to reduce crime, disorder and antisocial behaviour.
The principal public agency for conducting criminal prosecutions in England and Wales, established under the Prosecution of Offences Act 1985.
The unitary local authority for the Borough of Darlington in the Tees Valley.
The UK government department responsible for education and children's services in England.
note: RCVDA static list uses 'DoE / Department of Education'; the correct current name is Department for Education (DfE).

definition: An administrative code recording that a patient missed a booked appointment without notice; increasingly reframed as 'was not brought' for children.
The statutory duty on relevant partners to co-operate in safeguarding and promoting the wellbeing of adults (and, for children, under separate provisions).
note: Confirm intended sense: adult-safeguarding co-operation (Care Act 2014 s.6) vs children (Children Act 2004 s.10) vs the planning duty (Localism Act 2011 s.110).

definition: A framework of environmental, social and governance criteria used to assess an organisation's wider impact and responsible practice.
The unitary local authority for the Borough of Hartlepool in the Tees Valley.
A statutory local-authority committee bringing together the NHS, public health, adult social care and children's services to improve health and wellbeing and reduce inequalities.
source: Health and Social Care Act 2012, s.194

definition: A local executive group supporting the delivery of a Health and Wellbeing Board's priorities.
note: Appears to be a South Tees / local body — confirm exact remit.

definition: An approach to public policy that systematically accounts for the health implications of decisions across all sectors, to improve health and reduce inequalities.
source: World Health Organization — Health in All Policies.

definition: A statutory advocate who represents and supports a person who lacks capacity to make certain serious decisions and has no-one else appropriate to consult.
A geographical management area of Jobcentre Plus, the part of the Department for Work and Pensions that delivers working-age benefits and employment support.
source: Department for Work and Pensions — Jobcentre Plus.

definition: The Department for Education's statutory safeguarding guidance that schools and colleges in England must have regard to.
The national governing body for tennis in Great Britain.
note: Companies House: Lawn Tennis Association Limited, 07459469 (the national governing body, Roehampton). From the RCVDA static glossary's 'Others — commonly used in Sport' list.

term: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity
full_term: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity
definition: A Universal Credit determination that a claimant's health condition or disability so limits them that they are not expected to work or prepare for work, attracting an additional UC element.
source: Welfare Reform Act 2012; Universal Credit Regulations 2013

definition: A body that supports, develops and represents the local voluntary and community sector (for example a council for voluntary service); RCVDA is the LIO for Redcar & Cleveland.
The former statutory body coordinating local safeguarding of children; replaced from 2019 by multi-agency safeguarding arrangements led by three safeguarding partners.
note: Superseded by multi-agency safeguarding arrangements (Children and Social Work Act 2017).

definition: A person-centred, outcomes-focused approach to adult safeguarding that works with the person to achieve the outcomes they want. Distinct from My Sister's Place (also 'MSP').
source: Local Government Association / ADASS — Making Safeguarding Personal; reflected in Care Act 2014 statutory guidance.
note: Homonym: not My Sister’s Place (see my-sister-s-place-msp).

definition: The Act that provides the legal framework for making decisions on behalf of adults who lack the capacity to make particular decisions for themselves.
The Act governing the assessment, treatment and rights of people with a mental disorder, including detention ('sectioning') in hospital.

term: Mental Health Act Code of Practice
full_term: Mental Health Act Code of Practice
definition: The statutory guidance on how the Mental Health Act 1983 should be applied, which professionals must have regard to.
source: Department of Health (2015), under Mental Health Act 1983, s.118

definition: The statutory arrangements through which police, probation and prison services jointly assess and manage the risks posed by violent and sexual offenders.
The recognised body responsible for governing and regulating a particular sport nationally.

full_term: National Association for Voluntary and Community Action
definition: The national membership body for local infrastructure organisations supporting the voluntary and community sector in England.

The national body that led the NHS in England and oversaw commissioning; its functions are being brought back into the Department of Health and Social Care following the March 2025 decision to abolish it.
note: Confirm current transition status; NHS England abolition announced March 2025, phased over ~2 years.

definition: The NHS foundation trust providing 999 emergency and patient-transport ambulance services across the North East, including South Tees.
source: North East Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust

definition: A non-means-tested benefit that helps with the extra costs of a long-term health condition or disability; it replaced Disability Living Allowance for working-age adults.
The bodies that set standards for, accredit or regulate a profession or field of practice.
A multi-agency group that shares intelligence and coordinates action on the quality and safety of local health and care services.
source: NHS England — Quality Surveillance Group guidance.

definition: A non-profit provider of social housing (typically a housing association) registered with, and regulated by, the social housing regulator.
note: Now more commonly 'registered provider of social housing'.

definition: The statutory multi-agency board that oversees and coordinates adult safeguarding arrangements in a local area (locally, the Teeswide Safeguarding Adults Board).
A statutory review a Safeguarding Adults Board must arrange when an adult with care and support needs dies or is seriously harmed and abuse or neglect is suspected, to identify learning.

Local arrangements to provide emergency accommodation for people sleeping rough during severe weather; a discretionary, non-statutory response prompted by cold-weather and other severe-weather thresholds.
source: MHCLG rough sleeping / cold weather provision guidance.

full_term: Specific, Meaningful, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound, Evaluate, Re-adjust
definition: A goal-setting mnemonic extending the SMART objectives framework with 'Evaluate' and 'Re-adjust' stages.
A quality standard for supported-employment services helping disabled people and those with health conditions into work.
The sustainable-transport charity and custodian of the National Cycle Network; 'Sustrans' is short for 'sustainable transport'.
note: Registered charity 326550, now named Walk Wheel Cycle Trust (formerly Sustrans).

definition: A coordinated, person-centred approach bringing the relevant workers around one individual to plan and deliver joined-up support.
The rural community council for the Tees Valley, supporting rural communities and voluntary organisations.
A group-based, participative approach to treatment in which the community itself is the primary therapeutic agent, used in mental-health, substance-use and offender settings.
source: Royal College of Psychiatrists — Community of Communities.

full_term: Timely, Helpful, Respectful, Innovative, Values-based and Efficient
definition: A values mnemonic describing how services aim to work. Distinct from the local Thrive Partnership.
note: Homonym: not the Thrive Partnership (see thrive-partnership).

definition: The coordinated management of a town centre's environment, economy and activity, usually as a partnership between the local authority, businesses and other stakeholders.
The single means-tested working-age benefit that replaces six legacy benefits including Housing Benefit, Income Support and tax credits.
An umbrella term for a range of abuses disproportionately affecting women and girls, including domestic abuse, sexual violence, stalking and so-called honour-based abuse.
source: Home Office — Tackling Violence Against Women and Girls Strategy (2021).

definition: Charities, community groups and other not-for-profit organisations; the narrower predecessor term to VCSE (which also includes social enterprise).
The regional infrastructure body representing and supporting the voluntary, community and social enterprise sector across the North East.
